# Plot Descriptions — FCC Coral Health Report

**Site:** Farallon (S2P2), Cap Cana · **Generated by:** `code/analysis.r`
**Format:** JPEG, 300 DPI, A4 landscape (11.69 × variable inches)

All plots use the Wes Anderson "Moonrise3" colour palette. Species are colour-coded consistently across figures.

---

## 01_community_cover.jpeg

**Title:** Community coral cover — Farallon site (S2P2)

**Two-panel stacked figure:**

- **Top (pC1) — Stacked area chart:** Total coral cover over time broken down by species. The y-axis shows % of plot area (each 5×5m plot = 250,000 cm²). Each coloured band represents one species' contribution to total cover. Allows reading both the total cover trend and the species-level composition simultaneously.

- **Bottom (pC2) — Per-plot trajectories with model trend:** Individual plot total cover trajectories (thin grey lines) with a fitted LMM trend line (bold) and 95% confidence ribbon. The model (`log(% cover) ~ time_days + (1|plot_id)`) captures the site-level cover trajectory while accounting for plot-level variation.

**Key finding:** Total coral cover is increasing significantly over the monitoring period (model: β = +0.0004 log-units/day, p = 0.009).

---

## 02_species_growth_trajectories.jpeg

**Title:** Species growth trajectories

**Two-panel stacked figure:**

- **Top (pG1) — Mean colony area per species over time:** Faceted by species (one panel per species). Points show observed mean colony area ± SE at each survey date. The fitted line and ±30% band come from the base LMM (`log(area) ~ time_days × class + time_days × size_z`) evaluated at mean initial size (size_z = 0). Shows whether each species' average colony is growing, stable, or shrinking.

- **Bottom (pG2) — Per-species annual growth rate:** A dot-and-error-bar plot showing the LMM-estimated annual growth rate per species, back-transformed to % per year: `(exp(slope × 365) − 1) × 100`. Error bars are asymmetric ±1 SE back-transformed through the exponential (correct on the log scale). Species are sorted by growth rate. Significance labels from the model.

**Key finding:** Significant positive growth (`time_days` p < 0.001). PAST is the reference; CNAT and PSTR are significantly smaller at baseline.

---

## 03_turnover_balance.jpeg

**Title:** Growth vs. tissue loss balance per species

**Single horizontal bar chart (pT1):** Diverging bars show the mean annual % of colony area **gained** (green, rightward) and **lost** (red, leftward) per species per year. Values are normalised to previous colony area to allow fair comparison across species of different sizes: `(Δarea / prev_area) × 100 / days × 365`. The black dot shows net change (gained − lost) with ±SE error bar. Species ordered by net change.

**Why % rather than cm²/year:** Absolute cm²/year would conflate species with naturally large colonies (e.g. SINT, SSID) with fast growers. Percentage normalises for colony size and makes species directly comparable.

**Key finding:** All species show more gained than lost on average (net positive), consistent with the cover increase seen in plot 01.

---

## 04_initial_size_effects.jpeg

**Title:** Initial colony size as explanatory factor

**Two-panel side-by-side figure:**

- **Left (pS1) — Initial size vs. subsequent growth rate:** Each point is one colony; x-axis is initial size z-score (within species, 0 = species mean), y-axis is empirical % growth rate per year computed from first to last observation. The bold model line shows the predicted relationship from the LMM `time_days:size_z` interaction (PAST reference). The negative slope means larger initial colonies grow proportionally slower.

  This is the key visualisation of **ontogenetic growth slowdown** — a universal coral life-history pattern. Small colonies invest in competitive expansion; large established colonies grow more slowly in relative terms. The effect is statistically robust (t = −5.56, p < 0.001).

- **Right (pS2) — Size class composition per species:** Stacked bar chart showing the proportion of observations falling into small, medium, and large initial size classes (log-range thirds within species). Reveals whether species differ in their size structure — relevant for interpreting the overall species-level results (a species that is mostly small will have a different trajectory than one that is mostly large).

---

## 05_mortality_risk.jpeg

**Title:** Colony mortality risk — species and initial size

**Two-panel side-by-side figure:**

- **Left (pM1) — Survival probability by species (Tukey CLD):** Model-estimated probability of complete colony death per species, from a binomial GLMM (`fate_binary ~ size_z + class + (1|plot_id)`). Points are marginal means ± 95% CI. Compact letter display (Tukey) identifies significantly different groups — species sharing a letter are not statistically distinguishable. Y-axis is probability scale (%).

  **Key finding:** PAST has the lowest complete mortality probability, significantly lower than CNAT.

- **Right (pM2) — Size effect on mortality severity:** Scatter of all mortality events (partial and complete) against initial size z-score. Complete colony death events (area lost = 100%) are shown in dark brown; partial mortality events in red. The bold model line is from the LMM `log(partial_mortality) ~ size_z + class`, back-transformed with `exp()`. The dashed line marks the 100% complete-death threshold.

  **Key finding:** Larger initial colonies lose proportionally less area when mortality occurs (size_z β = −0.23, p = 0.011). The negative slope is visible in the scatter and confirmed by the model line.

  **Note:** Complete and partial mortality are treated as the same continuous variable (% area lost), with complete death simply being the 100% endpoint. This is ecologically appropriate — complete death is the extreme case of the same tissue-loss process.

---

## 06_appendix_species_size.jpeg

**Title:** Species biology reference

**Two-panel side-by-side figure:**

- **Left (p3) — Mean colony area bubble chart:** Grid of circles where each row is a species and each column is a size class (small / medium / large). Circle area is proportional to mean colony area (cm²) for that species × size class cell. White label inside each circle = number of individual colonies. Below each circle = actual mean area value (cm²). The top "All species" row summarises size-class totals across all species. Species rows are ordered by mean area (smallest at bottom).

  Significance annotations next to species names indicate whether mean colony area differs significantly from PAST (reference) based on the base LMM.

- **Right (pA2) — Tukey CLD dotplot:** Model-estimated geometric mean colony area per species (back-transformed from emmeans on the log scale) with 95% confidence intervals. Compact letter display from pairwise Tukey contrasts — species sharing a letter are not significantly different in mean size.

**Purpose:** Reference panel documenting baseline species biology. Shows both the absolute size differences between species and the statistical groupings, providing context for interpreting growth and mortality results.

---

## Notes on all figures

- **Colour palette:** Wes Anderson "Moonrise3" — consistent species colouring across all panels.
- **Model reference level:** *Porites astreoides* (PAST) throughout — chosen for highest colony count and lowest SE.
- **Low power species:** CNAT, PSTR, SSID, SINT all have n < 26 colonies (below d=0.8, power=0.80 threshold). Results for these species should be interpreted with caution; effect sizes are large but confidence intervals are wide.
- **Export settings:** 300 DPI JPEG, A4 landscape (297 × 210mm / 11.69 in wide), suitable for direct print inclusion.
